options.label: Discuss more first

options.label: New BK item + RFC-0021 (Recommended)
options.description: A new BK item (open, blocks BK-389's resume and so BK-394) with RFC-0021 as its design record. The RFC states the model; spec 003 and the kernel change only after it is accepted.

options.label: Amend RFC-0017
options.description: Add the model as a section of RFC-0017 (the kernel RFC) under BK-389. Keeps one record, but RFC-0017 is already accepted design for the kernel and grows a second subject.

options.description: A research note under sdd/research/ with no item yet; decide tracking once the model's shape is agreed. Cheapest, but nothing in the backlog records that #1127 is blocked.

questions.question: What should the first draft of the model cover?

options.label: Both layers, prose + table (Recommended)
options.description: Layer 1 (key set, geometry parameters, resolution outcomes incl. 'changed under the walk', per-op outcome→result tables) and layer 2 (per geometry: which driver observations reveal which outcome). The Dafny extension is named as a follow-up, not drafted.

options.label: Layer 1 only
options.description: The pure logical model and per-op tables first; the observation layer (where threads 1-2 live) in a second pass. Smaller, but threads 1-2 stay unanswerable until pass two.

options.label: Both layers + Dafny
options.description: Also extend BackendContract.dfy with flat and implicit geometries and a Resolve function. Strongest, but the largest; Dafny verification runs only via Docker here.

questions.question: On a flat store, a key can be a file and a prefix at once. How should the model treat that?

options.label: Own outcome FileAndPrefix (Recommended)
options.description: A first-class flat outcome with its own row; each op family states it explicitly (read: the file; list: the prefix; is_folder: True). Matches today's behaviour and makes the 'file ranks first' rule visible.

options.label: Normalise: file wins
options.description: Resolution reports File and the prefix is reachable only via folder-read ops. Simpler table, but is_folder/delete_folder must special-case the hidden prefix.

options.label: Forbid it in the model
options.description: Treat shadowing as an invalid store state, outside the contract. Simplest model, but S3-like stores produce it and today's spec defines answers for it.

questions.question: Where do links (follow_links) live?

options.label: A view parameter (Recommended)
options.description: resolve(S, key, view) with view = follow | no-follow; under no-follow a link is a non-folder entry (today's delete_folder rule). Keeps the outcome set small.

options.label: A separate outcome
options.description: Link is always its own outcome and every family states its column. More explicit, larger table.

questions.question: Is 'Absent at depth i' needed, or just 'Absent'?

options.label: Keep depth (Recommended)
options.description: Explicit-parents writes need where creation starts, and the observation layer needs it to say what an ancestor stat proved. Results for every other family ignore it.

options.label: Plain Absent
options.description: Depth becomes a write-route detail in layer 2. Smaller layer 1, but ensure_parents' contract leaves the model.

questions.question: Where should the outcome→result tables live?

options.label: One new spec section (Recommended)
options.description: A single 'Key resolution' section in spec 003 holds layer 1 + layer 2; per-op clauses keep only their result column and link to it (single source of truth).

options.label: A new spec file
options.description: A standalone spec (e.g. 0NN-key-resolution.md) that spec 003 and spec 013 cite. Cleaner boundary, one more file every op clause depends on.

options.label: A view parameter (Recommended)
options.description: resolve(S, key, view); under no-follow a link is a non-folder entry and lands in the File row. Only delete_folder asks for no-follow. The walk's 'never descend into a link' stays a layer-2 driver obligation.

questions.question: Absence in layer 1, given the code shows no result depends on depth?

options.label: Plain Absent / Blocked (Recommended)
options.description: Layer 1 has Absent and Blocked without depth. Layer 2 records which ancestor stat proved it; Blocked carries the file ancestor only as diagnostic data for the message.

options.label: Keep depth in layer 1
options.description: Absent(i) and Blocked(i) stay in the logical model, e.g. to leave room for a future op that needs it. Larger table for no current result.

questions.question: Does the three-part split (driver-declared link axis, store-level policy, fixed no-follow for destructive tree ops) match what you meant?

options.label: Yes, as tabled (Recommended)
options.description: Links become a geometry axis; the store picks a policy at construction with default follow_within_root; recursive delete always no-follow. Per-method follow_links stays internal (kernel↔driver only).

options.label: Store policy covers all ops
options.description: No fixed carve-out: a store set to follow also follows in delete_folder. Simpler rule, but a recursive delete can reach a link's target.

options.label: Per-method after all
options.description: A follow_links kwarg on public methods; resolution depends on the call. Most flexible, breaks resolve-as-function-of-state.

questions.question: How far should the RFC go on the public side of links?

options.label: Model only, public option later (Recommended)
options.description: The RFC defines the axis, the policy and the write-through-link cell; the store-level option and a public capability are a follow-up item. Keeps the RFC on the resolution model that unblocks #1127.

options.label: Include the public option
options.description: The RFC also designs the Store/Backend constructor option and the capability flag. One record, but adds a published-surface design to the critical path of #1127.

With is_file/is_folder mutually exclusive (file ranks first), how should folder operations treat a flat key that is both a file and a prefix?

options.label: Probes exclusive, folder ops see prefix (Recommended)
options.description: Mutual exclusivity binds the probes only. Folder-read and delete_folder address the prefix k/ (today's behaviour, BE-031 line 1629 unchanged). The model states it: on flat, a folder op names a prefix, not a node. No behaviour change.

options.label: File ranks first everywhere
options.description: A shadowed key is a file for every op: list_files(k) empty, delete_folder(k) InvalidPath. Fully consistent with the probes, but the prefix's entries become unreachable through k (only via the parent listing) and BE-031's row changes: a behaviour change.

options.label: Refuse ambiguity
options.description: Folder ops on a shadowed key raise InvalidPath naming the ambiguity. Explicit, but a behaviour change and a new error case for S3-like stores.

options.label: Keep it, error path only

options.label: Replace the link
options.description: The link is overwritten by a regular file. Matches 'a link is a file-like entry' literally, but loses the link without a signal.

options.label: Leave open
options.description: Keep it as an open question in the RFC; decide with the public link option follow-up.

questions.question: On a flat store with the file-ancestor policy on, what does a read of f/x answer when f is a file? (Open question 3)

options.label: Its own key (Recommended)
options.description: Blocked on flat applies to write targets only: the policy guards writes, and a read of f/x written by another tool still finds it. No extra probe on flat reads.

options.label: NotFound (Blocked)
options.description: With the policy on, the store behaves hierarchically for reads too: f/x is unreachable. Consistent, but costs an ancestor walk on every flat read with the policy on.

Should a flat store refuse to create the 'k is a file and k/ holds entries' state itself?

options.label: Opt-in, both directions (Recommended)
options.description: Extend the existing store policy so that, when on, it refuses both writing under a file and writing a file over a non-empty prefix. Default stays off: no new request on default writes, no breaking change. FileAndPrefix stays a defined outcome either way (D4).

options.label: Default on, both directions
options.description: Flat stores behave hierarchically for writes by default: FileAndPrefix arises only from foreign writers. Costs a stat per ancestor plus a list_page(limit=1) on every flat write; breaking for callers who rely on it today.

options.label: Status quo
options.description: Keep the one-direction opt-in (under a file only); writing a file over a non-empty prefix stays unguarded. The RFC records the asymmetry.

questions.question: Rewrite RFC-0021 around one abstract tree plus a partial abstraction function per backend encoding?

options.label: Yes, rewrite (Recommended)
options.description: Layer 1 = the tree (root folder, folders, items as leaves; a key names at most one node); each backend gets an abstraction function; geometry moves to the encoding; layer 2 and the family table survive with three outcomes.

options.label: Discuss more first
options.description: Keep exploring the reframing before the RFC is touched.

questions.question: A raw entry that does not decode to the tree (k/a.txt below item k, a backslash key): reachable or not?

options.label: Not in the store (Recommended)
options.description: Omitted from listings and logged, not reachable by key, only through unwrap(): BK-399's existing treatment, extended to every undecodable raw state. read('k/a.txt') answers NotFound. A behaviour change for flat backends.

options.label: Reachable by its own key
options.description: Omitted from listings but read/delete by exact key still work. Pragmatic for cleaning up such buckets, but the model then has nodes outside the tree.

questions.question: Should writes that would make the encoding undecodable be refused always?

options.label: Always refused (Recommended)
options.description: Writing below an item, or an item over a non-empty folder, is InvalidPath on every backend: a model invariant, not a policy. Costs a stat per ancestor plus a list_page(limit=1) on flat writes; replaces BE-008's opt-in.

options.label: Opt-in as today
options.description: Default off keeps flat writes cheap, but the store itself can then produce undecodable states, which the model must answer for.

questions.question: Does an emptied folder exist?

options.label: Encoding-dependent, stated (Recommended)
options.description: The tree allows empty folders; an encoding without folder objects cannot hold one, so a folder emptied there vanishes. Recorded as the one capability-like property of an encoding (no new op creates empty folders).

options.label: Folders exist only while non-empty
options.description: One rule everywhere: the kernel removes or hides an emptied folder on encodings with folder objects too. Uniform, but changes Local/SFTP behaviour and needs extra calls after deletes.

options.label: Listings strict, lookups trust (Recommended)
options.description: Listings omit undecodable entries (free: visible in the listing) and folder ops stat the key (D4's one stat). options.label: Strict, opt-in per store
options.description: Trusting lookups by default; a store-level option turns on the ancestor walk for keyed calls. Two behaviours to document and test.

Impact section (findings: row 1 'Today' cell false for item-over-folder; row 2 wrong for a\b and cost assumes OQ order; missing link changes, public kwarg retirement vs 'no public API change', spec timing for non-kernel backends, get_folder_info). How?

options.description: Split row 1 (below an item: written unless opt-in; item over folder: always written today); scope row 2 to item+prefix with cost conditional on the listing-order question; add SFTP link rows; state the kwarg retirement as a public API change, keeping BE-008's text for backends until each migrates; add get_folder_info to row 3.

options.description: Same, but the kwarg stays as a no-op/deprecated alias so 'no public API change' holds; the invariant applies regardless.

questions.question: A.8 probe rules (rule 1 forbids BE-030's success-path determinants; rule 3's two classes overlap; per-encoding (call, shape) tables announced but not drafted). How?

options.label: Fix rules, tables before acceptance (Recommended)
options.description: Carry BE-030's determinant list into A.8 and widen rule 1; restate rule 3 by timing (runs regardless → fails closed; runs only because the call refused → fails open, BE-021's wording); add the tables as an open question owned by BK-432, to be drafted before acceptance, and drop Impact's 'A.8 settles' claim until then.

options.label: Fix rules, draft tables now
options.description: Same rule fixes, and draft the per-encoding tables in this PR. Complete, but a large addition with its own review.

questions.question: Model gaps (flat delete/read of k/a.txt under an item: A.5 vs A.3; write/delete on a link: A.7 vs A.5, 'destructive tree operations' unlisted; dangling/escaping links missing from A.2/A.3; 'no operation creates an empty folder' unproven). How?

options.label: Resolve as proposed (Recommended)
options.description: A.5's through-an-item row is hierarchical; on flat, keyed families (probe, read-file, delete-file) trust the encoding, so delete('k/a.txt') removes the raw entry (the cleanup path). Destructive tree ops = delete_folder only; delete(link) removes the link; A.5's Item write cell notes the no_follow link exception. Dangling and escaping links decode to nothing: listings omit them, keyed calls answer Nothing. Empty-folder sentence narrowed to measured cases.

options.label: Discuss each first
options.description: Go through these four gaps one by one before editing.

options.label: Fix all (Recommended)
options.description: Retag the revise step ok with the miss in its extract; name the SFTP question; add to A.10 that the fake must emit an entry and same-named prefix on one page; add BE-017 to BK-432; drop user.api from the trace audience (proposal only, no CHANGELOG), keeping library.maintainer and contributor.process.

options.label: Fix all, keep user.api
options.description: Same, but keep user.api and add an Unreleased CHANGELOG line announcing the RFC.
